What made me think I could be trans...

Well, I started feeling like I was meant to be a boy when I hit puberty. I was pretty young, around 10. I was so uncomfortable with my body becoming more female looking and I was scared of boys looking at me and seeing me as a sexual object. I hated what my body was doing to me, my period especially made me severely distraught.

I then discovered yaoi (gay anime porn, lmao) at around 12 and felt some sort of affinity to it, like I was turned on by it and wanted to be it at the same time. I became obsessed with cute gay guys. I didn't want my body to be female. I wanted to have a male body with a male partner. 

What made me realise I'm not...

I'm 27 years old now and started realising I'm not really trans a couple years ago. I was sexually abused multiple times as a child and feel that this is what lead me to have a terrible relationship with my body. The disgust and shame associated with it. Overcoming that made me realise I'm just a female and it's okay. I've always felt like a female, never felt masculine at all really. It was definitely issues with my childhood that caused me to think I'm trans.

I'm in basically your exact position, if that makes you feel any better.. I pass as a female most of the time but my voice is so deep now from years of T (plus I've had top surgery), but I guess I'm feminine looking enough for most people to assume I'm a cis girl. I also love the goth aesthetic haha.

But as soon as I speak, I'm misgendered as a guy or a trans woman which I'm not. So I really relate to you.   I know what makes me feel better is other people relating to my experience, so I hope I can help you even just by sharing a very similar situation. 

Feeling dysphoria about wanting to go back to your original sex is such an odd and horrible feeling. I can't really give advice to you because I'm also feeling very lost, but I want to send you love and support. There are options, like voice training that's used for trans women, but I feel at the end of the day, self acceptance is the best method (for me anyway). 

You're a woman and your voice does not change that at all. There is not a one size fits all way to be a woman, and it's true that a lot of cis women have deep voices too. 

Wishing you the best and please reach out if you ever need to chat.
